`. Some tags, like `` for images, are self-closing.

Every HTML document starts with `<!DOCTYPE html>` to declare its type, followed by the root `<html>` element. Inside `<html>`, you'll find two main sections: `<head>`, which holds metadata like the page title and links to stylesheets, and `<body>`, which contains all the visible content you see in your browser. This includes all your headings, paragraphs, images, and links.

Elements often have attributes, like `href` for links or `src` for images, which provide extra information. A common pitfall for beginners is forgetting to close tags or nesting them incorrectly, leading to unexpected display issues. Always ensure your tags are properly closed and nested for a well-formed webpage.
